zhanghu-railway-resettlement.title: ZhangHu railway: 1,446 households relocated and RMB 67 million of compensation unpaid at closing
zhanghu-railway-resettlement.place: Wanquan District and Huai'an County, Zhangjiakou, Hebei, with works also in Hohhot and Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, China
zhanghu-railway-resettlement.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on Wanquan District of Zhangjiakou, where three households refused the compensation offered and the district government retained replacement apartments for them (OpenStreetMap place point for Wanquan District). The railway runs from Zhangjiakou in Hebei through Ulanqab to Hohhot in Inner Mongolia, and land was taken in 116 villages across 10 counties and districts.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: ZhangHu Railway Project, P122319. Loan IBRD-81310 (Loan 8131-CN) of US$200 million, approved 15 March 2012, effective 3 August 2012, mid-term review 28 October 2016, restructured 9 May 2018 to extend the closing date, original closing 30 June 2018, actual closing 30 June 2020. US$192,577,450 was disbursed. Total project cost was US$4,714,627,450 at completion against US$4,682,230,000 at appraisal, so the Bank financed about four per cent; the rest came from the borrower. Environmental category A. The loan triggered the Bank's policy on involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12). The completion report of 30 June 2021 rated the outcome Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory and M&E quality Modest, and rated land acquisition and resettlement as implemented moderately satisfactorily. The Independent Evaluation Group's review, ICRR0022658, rated the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, saying the project did not achieve improved accessibility and mobility of freight transport and so only partly achieved its objective, and rated Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory, M&E quality Modest and the quality of the completion report Substantial.

companies.name: Huzhang Railway Passenger Dedicated Line Co., Ltd.
companies.role: Project implementation unit. The completion report describes it as a joint venture company negotiated by the former Ministry of Railways, the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region and the Hebei Provincial Government, with Hohhot Railway Bureau, Inner Mongolia Communications Investment Co., Ltd. and Zhangjiakou Tongtai Holding Group Co., Ltd. as the representatives of the investors; it was registered on 10 October 2013 and is responsible for the construction and management of the ZhangHu railway. It assigned designated staff to manage land acquisition and resettlement and retained an external monitoring company to report on compensation payments. Under the approved financing plan Hebei Province and the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region each undertook the work and the cost of land acquisition and demolition in their own territory.

companies.name: China Railway Corporation
companies.role: Named in the completion report data sheet as the implementing agency. Its Department of Materials Management carried out the procurement financed by the Bank loan, with the assistance of a tendering company. The report also refers to it as the former China Railway Corporation, which put up RMB 13.151 billion of the project's registered capital.

zhanghu-railway-resettlement.community: The railway took 14,867 mu of land, 57 per cent of it farmland. The completion report states that the land acquisition affected 7,416 households in 116 villages, 10 counties and districts and 29 townships across three municipalities, Hohhot and Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia and Zhangjiakou City in Hebei. It resulted in the demolition of 396,969 square metres of houses and the relocation of 1,446 households. A further 168 enterprises, with 1,879 employees, were affected, and 6,717 mu of land was temporarily occupied and restored after construction. Compensation agreements for land were signed between the county or city land resources bureau and the affected villages, with funds paid to the villages through townships and sub-districts; agreements for houses were signed with each household and paid directly. As of the closing date of 30 June 2020, compensation of RMB 2,156 million, about US$317 million, had been paid in full in Inner Mongolia, and 96 per cent of the RMB 1,664 million, about US$245 million, due in Hebei had been paid. Overall 97 per cent of the project's compensation had been paid and RMB 67 million in Hebei had not. The report gives two reasons, and gives the funding shortage as RMB 57 million in the sentence that introduces them and as RMB 56 million in the bullet that follows. Zhangjiakou Municipality had a funding gap of RMB 56 million for state-owned land, collectively owned land and water wells; the municipal government directed Wanquan District and Huai'an County to borrow RMB 30 million each from Zhangjiakou Bank to cover it, its wholly owned financing vehicle Zhangjiakou Transport Investment Company issued a letter of commitment, and the loan applications had started. Separately three households declined the compensation offered under the resettlement plan. The funds, based on a third-party evaluation, were held in escrow for them, the Wanquan District Government had retained replacement apartments of around 100 square metres each, several rounds of negotiation failed to reach agreement, and the report adds that the three households have houses or apartments elsewhere to live in. Three enterprises in Huai'an County also declined the compensation offered and two filed lawsuits; their funds were also in escrow, and the county government undertook to follow the court's directive if it set different amounts. The report says the Bank would continue to supervise these issues until they were fully addressed. The Independent Evaluation Group's review records that its discussion with the Bank task team showed the team was still following up with the borrower on the outstanding resettlement compensation payments more than a year after the project closed; that is a statement by Bank staff to the evaluators, not a document.
zhanghu-railway-resettlement.outcome: The loan closed on 30 June 2020 with 97 per cent of compensation paid and RMB 67 million outstanding in Hebei Province, covering a municipal funding shortfall of RMB 56 million and unresolved disputes with three households and three enterprises, two of which had gone to court. The two Bank documents disagree on the project's outcome: the completion report of 30 June 2021 rated it Satisfactory and the Independent Evaluation Group's review rated it Moderately Unsatisfactory.
zhanghu-railway-resettlement.displaced_label: households relocated, after demolition of 396,969 square metres of houses (World Bank completion report, 30 June 2021)
zhanghu-railway-resettlement.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 5,748 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. No figure matching 5,748 appears in the documents opened. The appraisal document gives two sets of its own: the main text says approximately 23 townships and 100 villages and communities in Hebei and Inner Mongolia would be affected, including approximately 7,500 persons, about 23 per cent of them from enterprises, and that of those affected approximately 3,600 people from 1,078 households would be relocated; its safeguards annex says the project was estimated to affect approximately 7,511 persons, that approximately 3,631 people from 1,078 households would be relocated, of whom only 133 people from 43 households were urban, and that the project would affect 1,763 people from 34 enterprises. The outcome in the completion report is 1,446 households relocated and 7,416 households affected by land acquisition. ICIJ's own method page states what its figures count: it looked for what Bank documents call project-affected people, searching them for the words "affected", "PAP" or "displaced"; where a document counted only households it looked up an average household size; it decided to include all impacts, temporary ones among them, and says the impact counted "can be as modest as losing less than 1 percent of their land or income". It drew mainly on resettlement plans written before the work was done. Its data stops at 31 December 2014.

The project built and improved road corridors in four Anhui municipalities: Anqing, Huaibei, Lu'an and Wuhu.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: China: Anhui Medium Cities Urban Transport Project, P111421. Loan IBRD-78810, approved 20 May 2010 at US$100 million, effective 9 November 2010, mid-term review 12 August 2013, restructured 21 June 2012, 15 June 2015, 26 January 2016 and 31 July 2017, original closing 31 January 2016, actual closing 31 December 2017. The loan was cut to US$77,641,815, all of which was disbursed. Total project cost was US$232,090,000 at completion against US$268,720,000 at appraisal. Environmental category B. The loan triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment (OP/BP 4.01), physical cultural resources (OP 4.11) and involuntary resettlement (OP/BP 4.12). The completion report of 28 December 2018 rated the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory and M&E quality Modest. The Independent Evaluation Group's review, ICRR0021546, gave the same three ratings and rated the quality of the completion report Substantial. The report records that one reason the closing date was extended was delay in land acquisition and resettlement.

companies.name: Anhui Project Management Office
companies.role: Provincial project office that ran the loan, named in the completion report as APMO and as the body to which the external monitoring consultant reported and which the Bank dealt with on resettlement problems. The report's data sheet names the implementing agencies as the Anhui Construction Management Offices and the Wuhu Transport Bureau, and the resettlement housing that the 405 Lu'an households were waiting for was being built by Lu'an Municipal Government, not by the project.

luan-huaibei-urban-transport-resettlemen.community: The project's road works required land and the demolition of housing in Huaibei and Lu'an. The completion report states that at project closing on 31 December 2017, 473 households, 68 in Huaibei and 405 in Lu'an, were still to be resettled to permanent housing. When the report was drafted in December 2018 the 68 in Huaibei and 284 in Lu'an had been resettled, and 121 households in Lu'an had still not been relocated to permanent housing: 65 were expected to move in August 2019 and 56 in 2020. The report gives the cause as delay in the construction of large-scale resettlement housing by Lu'an, where households affected by this project were to be settled alongside displaced people from other, domestic projects, so the project's resettlement houses were only a small part of those sites. On compensation the report says the external monitoring consultant found the transition subsidy was paid in conformity with local policy, that the affected people were compensated in time to rehabilitate their livelihoods, that the transitional support was paid twice over because the transitional period was extended, and that on local leasing market information the subsidy the remaining 121 households received was well sufficient to pay rent for housing similar to their original property. The consultant was to keep monitoring the unfinished resettlement and report to the Bank quarterly, and the Bank said it would keep tracking it under a later project, the Anhui Road Maintenance Innovation and Demonstration Project (P153173). At appraisal the project was to permanently acquire 2,060 mu, 137 hectares, across 15 villages and urban communities in 11 townships and urban community units in Anqing, Huaibei, Lu'an and Wuhu, two-fifths of it land growing rice. The delays ran the other way as well: works on Longhezhong Road and Xicheng Road in Lu'an were significantly delayed by the demolition and land acquisition process, the Tuohe bus maintenance yard in Huaibei was never built because of changes to the municipal land use plan and difficulties in land acquisition, and only 146 of the planned 248 off-street bus bays were built.
luan-huaibei-urban-transport-resettlemen.outcome: The loan closed on 31 December 2017 with 473 households not yet moved into permanent housing. A year later 121 households in Lu'an were still waiting, 56 of them with no move expected before 2020, which is about two years after the loan closed and some years after their homes were taken. The completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review agree on the ratings: outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory, M&E quality Modest.

It drew mainly on resettlement plans written before the work was done. Its data stops at 31 December 2014.

zhegan-line-railway-resettlement.title: Zhe-Gan railway upgrade: 7,573 families resettled against 2,666 planned
zhegan-line-railway-resettlement.place: The Zhe-Gan railway line through Zhejiang, Jiangxi and Hunan, China
zhegan-line-railway-resettlement.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on Yingtan in Jiangxi, a city on the Zhe-Gan line roughly midway along it (OpenStreetMap place point for Yingtan). The resettlement plan covered 560 villages in 133 townships in three provinces along 943 kilometres of railway, so no single point covers it; the plan was issued in separate Zhejiang, Jiangxi and Hunan volumes.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Second National Railways Project (Zhe-Gan Line), P075602. Loan IBRD-47460 of US$200 million, approved 24 June 2004, effective 16 January 2005, closed 31 January 2008 on the original closing date, with US$199.0 million disbursed. Environmental category A. The completion report, ICR0000918, is dated 15 August 2008 on its cover and 17 August 2008 in its own data sheet. It rated the outcome Satisfactory, risk to the development outcome Low or Negligible, Bank performance Satisfactory and borrower performance Highly Satisfactory. The Independent Evaluation Group's review, ICRR13032, posted 30 September 2008, gave the same outcome, risk, Bank performance and borrower performance ratings. The review rated the quality of the completion report Satisfactory while noting that the report "does not discuss the number of people resettled".

companies.name: Ministry of Railways, Foreign Capital and Technical Import Center
companies.role: The unit inside China's then Ministry of Railways that handled foreign-financed railway projects, named in the completion report as the implementing agency and abbreviated FCTIC. The report records that the ministry did not administer resettlement itself: that was done by local governments from the provincial level down to the village level, and the ministry's centre intervened when resettlement was delayed.

zhegan-line-railway-resettlement.community: The project raised speeds, renewed signalling and electrified the double-track Zhe-Gan line, and realigning the track shortened it from 942 to 916 kilometres. Annex 2 of the completion report sets the appraisal plan against the outcome. Land acquisition was planned at 26,668 mu and came to 31,800 mu. Resettlement was planned for 2,666 families and came to 7,573 families, nearly three times the plan. At appraisal the resettlement plan covered 560 villages in 133 townships in three provinces along 943 kilometres of line, and the appraisal document states that the project would affect 49,102 people, including 45,853 affected by land requisition and 2,666 households with 9,401 inhabitants subject to structure demolition, with 6,152 people affected by both. The report's own account of the resettlement is favourable: a completion mission visited five resettlement villages in five different counties in March 2008 and, after talking to resettled people, resettlement staff and local officials, concluded the resettlement had been completed successfully and that the affected people were satisfied with their compensation and other arrangements. Resettlement was monitored by Southwest Communication University, and people were compensated by redistribution of land, by an alternative site or in cash. The report also records that there were a few delays in resettlement caused by the administrative structure, in which the ministry pays and local government administers, and gives as a lesson that "On China railway projects this can lead to a disconnect between the project's Resettlement Action Plan and actual implementation." Neither Bank document explains why the number of families resettled came out at 7,573 against a plan of 2,666, and neither names a village where people moved.
zhegan-line-railway-resettlement.outcome: The loan closed on time on 31 January 2008 with the railway built. The completion report records 7,573 families resettled against 2,666 planned, and 31,800 mu of land taken against 26,668 mu planned, without accounting for the gap. The Independent Evaluation Group agreed with every rating the report gave and, in the same review, recorded as a shortcoming that the report does not discuss the number of people resettled, although Annex 2 of the report gives the number of families.

nanchang-line-2-demolition.title: Nanchang metro Line 2: private houses demolished and 170,468 square metres of land acquired along the corridor
nanchang-line-2-demolition.place: The Line 2 corridor between ZhanQianNanDaDao and XinJiaAn stations, Nanchang, Jiangxi, China
nanchang-line-2-demolition.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on Nanchang (OpenStreetMap place point for Nanchang). The works ran along the Line 2 corridor from ZhanQianNanDaDao station to XinJiaAn station; the documents do not name the neighbourhoods where houses were demolished.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: China: Nanchang Urban Rail Project, P132154. Loan IBRD-82620 (Loan 8262-CN), approved 20 June 2013 at US$250 million, effective 21 October 2013, mid-term review 13 February 2017, restructured 17 August 2018, original closing 31 October 2018, actual closing 31 December 2019. The loan was cut to US$189,492,846, all of which was disbursed. Total project cost was US$2,189,961,846 at completion against US$2,571,230,000 at appraisal. Environmental category A. The loan triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment (OP/BP 4.01), physical cultural resources (OP 4.11) and involuntary resettlement (OP/BP 4.12). A separate project component covered land acquisition and resettlement costs, financed entirely by the client and not by the Bank. The completion report of 31 December 2020 rated the outcome Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory and M&E quality Substantial. The Independent Evaluation Group's review, ICRR0022446, agreed on outcome and Bank performance and cut M&E quality to Modest for moderate shortcomings in the selection of indicators and limited information on data collection methodologies.

companies.name: Nanchang Urban Rail Group Co.
companies.role: Named in the completion report data sheet as the implementing agency and in its text as the URC. It prepared and carried out the resettlement plan, which was disclosed at its offices in January 2013, and the report records that it went on to apply the Bank's compensation and resettlement approach to the city's Lines 3 and 4. The completion report also records that it failed to coordinate utility relocation and traffic diversion effectively, which contributed to the delay in the works.

nanchang-line-2-demolition.community: Clearing the Line 2 corridor required demolition of housing and of commercial premises. The completion report states that resettlement work started in April 2013, that the demolition of private houses and the resettlement work connected with it was fully completed by August 2014, and that the enterprise structures were finished by the end of 2017. It then states: "Altogether 1344 urban families, 130 enterprises and 41 rural families were affected and 170,468.13m2 of land was acquired." The report says cash compensation and resettlement relocation housing were provided to the displaced families, and that 27 per cent of the affected families gained an improvement in their living environment; it gives no figure for the other families. Implementing the resettlement plan cost US$514 million, more than twice the US$193 million estimated at appraisal, and was funded entirely by the client. The report records that the final Bank supervision mission concluded the social safeguards were satisfactory, that nine external monitoring reports confirm the affected people were satisfied with the process, and that the relocation of the No. 28 High School was chosen as best practice for the Bank's Urban Rail Handbook for the measures taken to limit disruption to commuting and classroom schedules. At appraisal the figures were different and larger: acquisition of 746 mu of village land, 259 mu of it cultivated, affecting 142 people from 31 families; demolition of 83,817 square metres of structures owned by 1,043 families and affecting 4,001 people; and demolition of 201 shops and 22 enterprises and organisations. Neither document compares the appraisal count of 1,043 families with the completion count of 1,344 urban families and 41 rural families, and neither says how many of the 1,344 lost their homes as against their land. Resettlement of commercial entities along Line 2 was one of the reasons the closing date had to be extended.
nanchang-line-2-demolition.outcome: Line 2 opened and the loan closed on 31 December 2019. The demolition of private houses was completed by August 2014 and the demolition of enterprise structures by the end of 2017, and 170,468.13 square metres of land was acquired. The completion report of 31 December 2020 and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of 28 May 2021 both rate the project Satisfactory and both treat the resettlement as satisfactory; the review cuts the M&E rating to Modest.
nanchang-line-2-demolition.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 5,058 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. No figure matching 5,058 appears in the documents opened. The appraisal document gives 4,001 people affected by the demolition of 83,817 square metres of structures owned by 1,043 families, plus 142 people from 31 families affected by land acquisition and 201 shops and 22 enterprises and organisations to be demolished. The completion report's outcome figures are 1,344 urban families, 41 rural families and 130 enterprises, with 170,468.13 square metres of land acquired. The report uses the word "affected" for those counts and the words "displaced families" in the following sentence, and gives no separate count of households whose homes were demolished. No count of people or households relocated is given here, because no document gives one: the word attached to the 1,344 urban families in both Bank documents is "affected", and the families whose houses were demolished are not separated from those who lost only land. ICIJ's own method page states what its figures count: it looked for what Bank documents call project-affected people, searching them for the words "affected", "PAP" or "displaced"; where a document counted only households it looked up an average household size; it decided to include all impacts, temporary ones among them, and says the impact counted "can be as modest as losing less than 1 percent of their land or income". It drew mainly on resettlement plans written before the work was done. Its data stops at 31 December 2014.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Henan Towns Water Supply and Sanitation Project, P081348. henan-towns-water-land-acquisition.community: Land was taken in the suburbs of county towns to build water plants and wells. The completion report states that resettlement activities were carried out moderately satisfactorily, that a final report on resettlement implementation was prepared, "but there are inconsistencies in the data, which the PPMO has not been able to clarify." It gives the actual impacts as almost 660 mu of permanently acquired land, which affected 713 households or 2,834 people, and 300 square metres of residential housing demolition, which affected 4 households or 15 people. Annex 5 of the report sets out the 713 households and 2,834 people subproject by subproject across 20 water supply schemes, the largest being Lushan with 130 households and 520 people and Dengzhou with 87 households and 348 people, and totals 659.73 mu. Table 5.2 of the same annex, comparing planned with actual, gives the number of affected people as 1,041, not 2,834, and the actual permanent land acquisition as 644.95 mu, not 659.73; neither document reconciles either pair. On compensation the report says the rates for resettlement and land acquisition ended up higher than the rates agreed in the resettlement plan, "except for about 57.4 mu of land for which an annual rental fee is being paid". Land was also used temporarily to lay water pipes, mostly along main urban roads and returned to its owners shortly after installation, and farmers whose crops were affected were compensated under local government rules. The cost of land acquisition and resettlement fell from an estimate of RMB 97.67 million to about RMB 34.67 million, which the report attributes to subprojects in 17 participating counties being dropped from the project; Annex 5 gives the final figure as RMB 36.47 million. The Independent Evaluation Group's review repeats the report's resettlement account but leaves out the 57.4 mu paid for by annual rent, and so states without qualification that the compensation rates ended up higher than the rates agreed in the plan.
henan-towns-water-land-acquisition.outcome: The loan closed on 30 June 2013 rated Unsatisfactory by the Bank's own completion report, with 17 counties' subprojects dropped and benefits reaching substantially fewer people than expected at appraisal. The resettlement data the province submitted was internally inconsistent and the completion report says the province could not explain it. About 57.4 mu of land was still being paid for by an annual rental fee rather than compensated at the agreed rate when the report was written. The Independent Evaluation Group downgraded borrower performance to Unsatisfactory.
henan-towns-water-land-acquisition.displaced_label: households, 15 people, whose houses were demolished, 300 square metres in all, out of 713 households or 2,834 people recorded as affected by the land acquisition for the water plants and wells (World Bank completion report, 24 December 2013)
henan-towns-water-land-acquisition.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 3,995 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. No figure matching 3,995 appears in the documents opened, and the appraisal document gives land areas rather than a count of people. The completion report's own figures disagree with each other: the text and Table 5.1 of Annex 5 give 713 households or 2,834 people affected by land acquisition, while Table 5.2 of the same annex gives 1,041 affected people. The only count of people moved is 4 households, 15 people, whose houses, 300 square metres in all, were demolished. ICIJ's own method page states what its figures count: it looked for what Bank documents call project-affected people, searching them for the words "affected", "PAP" or "displaced"; where a document counted only households it looked up an average household size; it decided to include all impacts, temporary ones among them, and says the impact counted "can be as modest as losing less than 1 percent of their land or income". It drew mainly on resettlement plans written before the work was done. Its data stops at 31 December 2014.

sichuan-wudu-canal-resettlement.community: The project built part of the Xizi main canal, eleven branch canals and a reservoir at Jinfeng with a storage capacity of 98 million cubic metres. The completion report states that resettlement under the project included land acquisition and population relocation caused by the construction of the Jinfeng reservoir, the Xizi main canal and the branch and lateral canals, covering 14,408.04 mu, about 9.6 square kilometres, of land acquisition and 3,449 relocated people in 992 households. It adds that about 16,500 further people were affected by land acquisition to a limited extent in the canal areas. Resettlement plans were prepared, the resettlement was carried out in consultation with the affected people and monitored continuously by an external professional agency, and the report states that land acquisition and population relocation was completed satisfactorily by project closure, that the project-affected people were compensated on time and in full, and that the resettlement complied with the Bank's safeguard policy and with national law. At appraisal the figures were smaller: the appraisal document says the Bank-financed works would requisition about 4,245 mu of village land in 136 villages, 2,318 mu of it farmland, affecting about 3,848 farmers in 1,063 households, of whom 990 people in 264 households would lose their houses as well. The wider Wudu Phase II programme, of which the Bank financed a part, was to requisition 10,037 mu, remove 185,309 square metres of structures, relocate 3,525 people and require livelihood restoration for 4,716 people. The appraisal figure for people losing their houses was 990 in 264 households and the completion figure for people relocated is 3,449 in 992 households; neither document compares the two. Three of the six project counties were in provincial-level poverty-tagged areas, and the project area had been hit by the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake.
sichuan-wudu-canal-resettlement.outcome: The loan closed on 31 October 2019 with 3,449 people in 992 households relocated. The completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review both record the resettlement as compliant and compensation as paid on time and in full, and neither records a shortfall, a complaint or a grievance. Neither document names a village from which people moved or a site to which they went.

A fifth project component, costed at US$35.00 million at appraisal and US$31.06 million at completion, paid for resettlement and environmental management. xining-riverway-house-demolition.community: The project carried out flood works and watershed management on the Huangshui and Nanchuan rivers and in the counties around Xining. The completion report states that resettlement was limited to Xining downtown areas and Hangyuan County and involved the acquisition of 1,635.1 mu, 108.7 hectares, of rural collective land in 39 villages, affecting 888 households comprising 3,549 people. It then states that urban riverway management activities involved house demolition and affected 132 households, 538 people, and that 22 enterprises or businesses on the banks of the Nanchuan and Huangshui rivers were affected. The report says the resettlement plan and a supplementary plan prepared at restructuring for newly added works were implemented in a satisfactory manner, that the resettlement was effective, that livelihoods of the affected people had been restored and that interviews showed farmers were highly satisfied with the compensation provided. Both counts are the appraisal document's, repeated unchanged; the completion report gives no separately measured outcome figure for either. The appraisal document gives the same two counts in advance: 1,635.1 mu to be acquired from 39 rural villages affecting 3,549 farmers in 888 households, and 538 people in 132 households to be relocated for house demolition, among them 313 people in 89 households affected by the loss of both land and housing. An Ethnic Minorities Development Plan was prepared for ethnic minorities in Datong, Huangyuan and Huangzhong counties, covering 21 ethnic minority communities and 8 communities where ethnic minorities predominate. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of the project's safeguards does not carry the figure of 132 households, and records separately that the key negative impact on minority groups, reduced grazing, was expected to be offset by reduced erosion and flooding, but that those positive effects would not be felt for at least three years.
xining-riverway-house-demolition.outcome: The loan closed on 31 December 2015. The completion report records the land acquisition and the urban riverway house demolition as carried out and the resettlement as satisfactory, and gives the same counts as the appraisal document: 1,635.1 mu taken in 39 villages, affecting 888 households, and house demolition affecting 132 households, 538 people. The fifth project component, which paid for resettlement and environmental management, spent US$31.06 million of the US$35.00 million budgeted. Neither document records an unpaid claim, a grievance or a complaint, and neither names a village or a street.

No count of people or households relocated is given here: the completion report's figures are the appraisal document's, repeated word for word, and the report's own verb for the 132 households is "affected" by house demolition. ICIJ's own method page states what its figures count: it looked for what Bank documents call project-affected people, searching them for the words "affected", "PAP" or "displaced"; where a document counted only households it looked up an average household size; it decided to include all impacts, temporary ones among them, and says the impact counted "can be as modest as losing less than 1 percent of their land or income". It drew mainly on resettlement plans written before the work was done. Its data stops at 31 December 2014.

yining-urban-roads-demolition.community: The project built and rebuilt urban roads in Yining. The completion report states that most project beneficiaries and affected people belong to the Uygur ethnic minority. Its Table 3 sets the resettlement plan against the outcome. Land acquisition was planned from 213 households over 980.75 mu and came to 166 households over 525.52 mu. House demolition was planned for 648 households over 94,964.74 square metres and came to 93 households over 14,585.63 square metres. The report attributes both reductions to design optimisation, and says that the road cross-sections were narrowed, land acquisition minimised and parallel roads consolidated. It also records that resettlement was slow: in some densely populated areas additional resettlement was needed, which delayed some road construction and rehabilitation, resettlement was rated moderately satisfactory around the mid-term review because of slow progress in building the resettlement site, and resettlement was eventually completed on time. An Ethnic Minority Development Plan was prepared, the appraisal document having recorded that ethnic minorities make up about 65 per cent of Yining city's population and Uygurs 49.7 per cent, and the report says it was implemented as planned. The appraisal document had set out 980 mu of land to be taken from 13 villages affecting 922 people in 213 households, 2,837 people in 648 households to be relocated by house demolition, and 130 shops or vendors and 21 enterprises and institutes to be affected.

shaying-river-sanba-village-resettlement.community: The project dredged and widened about 205.6 kilometres of the Shaying River channel for navigation, strengthened 43.87 kilometres of bank, rebuilt four bridges and added ship locks. The completion report states that by project closure all resettlement was complete except for one outstanding issue at Sanba village in Yingshang county, where 23 rural households had been resettled. In January 2018, after the loan closed, the Bank was informed that a large area of Sanba village, including the Sanba resettlement site itself, had been identified by the county government for economic development and that the 23 households would be moved to another site. Ten of the 23 took cash compensation and left. The remaining 13 chose to move to Xiayuan Resident Compound, a new site assigned by Yingshang county government, where construction was expected to be finished only by June 2019. Those 13 households were given an 18-month transition fee, which the report says is sufficient to rent houses in nearby towns. The report says the Bank remained committed to their satisfactory resettlement in compliance with Bank policy, that the provincial project office agreed to go on monitoring it under a later Bank-supported programme covering Fuyang municipality, that Yingshang County would provide six-monthly interim reports on the progress of the resettlement housing, that a grievance mechanism was being established so the 13 households could raise concerns with the provincial office, and that Bank social specialists would visit in early 2019 and June 2019. The report also records that land acquisition was delayed by weak coordination between the county land bureaus and the project company and by delays in agreeing the unit price for land compensation, and that new resettlement plans were prepared when additional land was required. On the wider picture it says the livelihoods of resettled households had been improved to a certain extent and that resettled households said the new bridge made their lives and travel more convenient. At appraisal the project was to take 1,658 mu, 111 hectares, permanently and 9,874 mu, 658 hectares, temporarily, to relocate 364 households involving 1,489 people, and to affect 2,891 households, 10,316 people, through temporary land use at 34 sites for dredged sediment, for a stated total of 3,679 households, 13,456 people, affected by resettlement. Neither Bank document gives an outcome count of households relocated across the whole project.
shaying-river-sanba-village-resettlement.outcome: The loan closed on 31 December 2017. A month later the Bank learned that the resettlement site built for the 23 Sanba village households had been designated by the county government for economic development, so the households had to move a second time. Ten took cash and left. Thirteen were renting housing in nearby towns on an 18-month transition fee, waiting for a new compound that was not expected to be finished before June 2019, about 18 months after the loan closed. Monitoring of their resettlement was transferred to a later Bank-financed programme. No document found records whether the 13 households moved in.
shaying-river-sanba-village-resettlement.displaced_label: rural households resettled at Sanba village whose resettlement site was then taken for economic development, of whom 10 took cash compensation and 13 were awaiting a second site (World Bank completion report, 18 June 2018)

No figure matching 3,140 appears in the documents opened. The appraisal document's own figures are 364 households, 1,489 people, to be relocated and 3,679 households, 13,456 people, affected by resettlement in total, most of that through temporary use of land for dredged sediment. The only household count in the completion report is the 23 at Sanba village; neither Bank document gives a project-wide outcome count of households relocated. ICIJ's own method page states what its figures count: it looked for what Bank documents call project-affected people, searching them for the words "affected", "PAP" or "displaced"; where a document counted only households it looked up an average household size; it decided to include all impacts, temporary ones among them, and says the impact counted "can be as modest as losing less than 1 percent of their land or income". It drew mainly on resettlement plans written before the work was done. Its data stops at 31 December 2014.

It is the clearest single harm in this set: households moved once for the project and then moved again when the county reassigned their new site. What is thin is the ending. The documents stop in mid-2018, with 13 households renting and a compound unfinished, and no later document was found that says whether they moved in. The favourable detail is given as the report gives it: the 18-month transition fee, which the report calls sufficient to rent in nearby towns, the grievance mechanism being set up, and the two Bank monitoring visits planned. No source outside the World Bank was found. Searches in English and in Chinese, including the village name in Chinese characters, returned no news report, court record, NGO field study or Inspection Panel complaint about this project. What is set out here is the lender reporting on its own project: the completion report, written by Bank staff with a borrower section, and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of that report, which is the Bank's own internal evaluation unit.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Chongqing Urban-Rural Integration Project, P086446. Loan IBRD-79200 (LN. 7920-CN), approved 3 June 2010 at US$84 million, effective 18 October 2010, mid-term review 22 March 2013, restructured 1 August 2013 and 17 December 2015, original closing 30 June 2016, actual closing 30 June 2017. The loan was cut to US$75,433,454, all of which was disbursed. Total project cost was US$159,776,364 at completion against US$191,850,000 at appraisal. Environmental category B. The loan triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment, involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12) and safety of dams (OP 4.37), the last of which ceased to apply. The completion report, ICR00004173, of 8 February 2018 rated the execution of resettlement activities moderately satisfactory, Bank quality of supervision Moderately Unsatisfactory and overall Bank performance Moderately Unsatisfactory. The Independent Evaluation Group's review, ICRR0021166, rated the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Unsatisfactory and M&E quality Modest, matching the completion report in every row.

companies.name: Chongqing Project Management Office
companies.role: Named in the completion report data sheet as the implementing agency and in its text as the PMO that oversaw the project implementation units in each county and district. The report records that the office and its units made frequent site visits, held public consultations and carried out door-to-door surveys of affected households, and that the project management consultant acted as the external monitoring agency for the resettlement plan.

tongliang-road-land-lease-compensation.community: The project built roads, water supply and village infrastructure across several counties and districts of Chongqing. The clearest recorded failure is in Tongliang. The borrower's account in Annex 7 of the completion report states that in Tongliang, because of complicated procedures and the land quota set by the state government, land for the road construction was initially compensated as a land lease; this was finally corrected to the Bank's requirements and all the villages and villagers were properly compensated for the land acquired under Bank policies. The report's assessment of Bank supervision records the timing: some issues stayed unresolved for a protracted period, among them the "resettlement issue in Tongliang, solved just at the loan closing although the works had been completed three years earlier." The Independent Evaluation Group's review repeats that the resettlement issue in Tongliang was solved at loan closing. On scale the report's body text and its own annex do not agree. The body text gives the actual resettlement impacts as 412.526 mu of permanently acquired land, which affected 593 households or 2,837 people, and 70 square metres of residential housing demolished, which affected seven houses and 25 people. Annex 7's table instead gives 309.194 mu acquired case by case, 322.526 mu acquired permanently and 90 mu allocated by government; 2,474.96 square metres of house demolition with 593 affected households and 2,387 project-affected people; and, in a separate column, seven impacted individual enterprises covering 70 square metres with 25 project-affected people. So the 70 square metres and the 25 people that the body text attributes to seven houses are, in the annex, seven enterprises, and the annex's figure of 2,387 people differs from the body text's 2,837 by a transposed pair of digits. Neither document explains either difference. The subprojects in the annex are the Yongchun roads, with 1,810 square metres demolished, 203 affected households and 899 people, the Tongliang roads with 52 households and 144 people, Qijiang New Countryside with 153 households and 602 people, and in Chengkou the water supply with 2 households and 10 people and the roads with 664.96 square metres, 183 households and 732 people. On the other side of the ledger the report says the compensation rates for resettlement and land acquisition exceeded the rates agreed in the resettlement plan, that compensation to each affected household was increased because land prices had risen and more favourable compensation policies had been issued, that compensation funds were issued without delay or deduction, that the independent monitoring consultant's survey found no project-affected people were pushed into poverty by the land acquisition and that for most of them incomes and living conditions improved, and that external monitoring reported the resettlement plan had limited impact on household incomes, livelihoods and farming because only a minor part of each holding was acquired. For the Wangliao Road in Yongchuan the affected people were paid RMB 36,000 per head in cash and a pension plan was bought for them paying RMB 500 a month per head with an annual increment, which the borrower says is much higher than their previous earnings from the land. The reported cost of land acquisition and resettlement is also given twice: the body text says the original estimate of US$50 million was much higher than the actual US$15 million, and Annex 7 says the final cost for compensation was around US$20 million at loan closing.
tongliang-road-land-lease-compensation.outcome: The loan closed on 30 June 2017 rated Moderately Unsatisfactory by the Bank's own completion report and by its Independent Evaluation Group. The Tongliang land compensation was put on the correct basis only at the moment of closing, three years after the road works there were finished. The completion report's body text and its own Annex 7 give different figures for how much land was taken, how many square metres of housing were demolished, how many people were affected and what the compensation cost, and neither document reconciles them.
tongliang-road-land-lease-compensation.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 2,912 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. No figure matching 2,912 appears in the documents opened; the appraisal document says resettlement impacts were modest and scattered, with about 3,300 people affected by land acquisition and house demolition and 1,200 mu, 80 hectares, of land acquired. No field for a count of people relocated is given here because the completion report's two accounts conflict: the body text records 70 square metres of residential housing demolished affecting seven houses and 25 people, while Annex 7 records 2,474.96 square metres of house demolition with 593 affected households and 2,387 project-affected people and puts the 70 square metres and 25 people against seven enterprises instead. ICIJ's own method page states what its figures count: it looked for what Bank documents call project-affected people, searching them for the words "affected", "PAP" or "displaced"; where a document counted only households it looked up an average household size; it decided to include all impacts, temporary ones among them, and says the impact counted "can be as modest as losing less than 1 percent of their land or income". It drew mainly on resettlement plans written before the work was done. Its data stops at 31 December 2014.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Poor Rural Communities Development Project, P071094. Loan IBRD-73100 of US$100.0 million, approved 21 June 2005, effective 15 December 2005, mid-term review 17 June 2008, original closing 31 December 2010, actual closing 30 June 2011, with US$99.71 million disbursed. Total project cost was US$163.86 million at completion against US$142.10 million at appraisal, 115 per cent of the estimate. Environmental category B. The project triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment (OP 4.01), indigenous peoples (OD 4.20) and involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12). The completion report, ICR1835, of 20 December 2011 rated the outcome Satisfactory, risk to the development outcome Moderate, Bank performance Satisfactory and borrower performance Satisfactory. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 27 January 2014 kept the Satisfactory outcome and Bank performance, raised the risk to the development outcome to Significant, citing uncertainty about continued technical support to project communities and about financing operation and maintenance after completion, and cut borrower performance to Moderately Satisfactory, citing the absence of strong central leadership and unclear responsibilities among provincial government offices. The report's cover names the trust funds TF-54747 and TF-55699 while its data sheet names TF-54949 and TF-70354.

lenders.name: Department for International Development, United Kingdom
lenders.role: Co-financier. The completion report states that DFID provided grant support for the project amounting to US$37 million, and that separate additional DFID grants paid for a free education pilot and for the independent monitoring. DFID staff took part in the supervision missions alongside the Bank.

companies.name: State Council Leading Group Office for Poverty Reduction
companies.role: Named in the completion report as an implementing agency alongside the Ministry of Finance and the Foreign Capital Project Management Offices of Guangxi, Sichuan and Yunnan. It is the body under China's State Council that runs national poverty reduction programmes; the report abbreviates the provincial poverty alleviation bodies PADO and records that the Guangxi and Luocheng county project offices took immediate corrective action after the Bank's fourth supervision mission in April 2007 found extreme deficiencies in institutional capacity in Luocheng County in Guangxi.

guangxi-poor-rural-land-acquisition.community: The project worked in 18 nationally designated poor counties in Guangxi, Sichuan and Yunnan, eleven of them ethnic minority autonomous counties, and built village access roads, health clinics, drinking water facilities and other village works. The completion report states that over 8,000 project households in Guangxi were affected by the acquisition of about 3,000 mu of land for the construction of village access roads, health clinics and drinking water facilities. Its account of how that land was obtained is favourable: most of the land needed for village-level works was voluntarily provided by the affected villages and villagers, the acquisition in Guangxi was carried out to the satisfaction of the affected people through participatory approaches, case study investigations suggest the affected people were satisfied with the arrangements and that their income levels rose by at least 50 per cent on average between 2004 and 2010, and all land acquisition was generally done in accordance with Chinese regulations and Bank policies. Against that the report records a finding by the Bank's own safeguards specialist: "agreement in writing was not always reached in advance with the PAPs when it was necessary to take their land in order to complete project civil works", and that compensation standards should be adequately discussed with and supported by the affected people and should be in line with local government regulations. The Independent Evaluation Group's review repeats the point in its own words, that agreement on land acquisition in writing was not always timely in reaching the affected people and that compensation standards needed to be more adequately explained to them. The appraisal document had anticipated that land acquisition would be limited and scattered and that "no physical relocation of people is anticipated to be necessary", and the completion report records none. The report also records what made the land easier to obtain: the participatory approach, early advance notice and community mobilisation, with communities and villagers voluntarily offering land once they understood that they would be the direct beneficiaries of the roads, water facilities and clinics built on it.
guangxi-poor-rural-land-acquisition.outcome: The loan closed on 30 June 2011 rated Satisfactory. Over 8,000 households in Guangxi had given up land, about 3,000 mu in all, and the Bank's safeguards specialist found that written agreement had not always been reached with them before the land was taken. The Independent Evaluation Group raised the risk to the development outcome to Significant and cut borrower performance to Moderately Satisfactory. Neither Bank document states what compensation those households received.
guangxi-poor-rural-land-acquisition.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 2,791 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. No figure matching 2,791 appears in the documents opened. No count of people relocated is given here because the appraisal document states that no physical relocation of people was anticipated and neither Bank document records any. The land figure in the completion report is over 8,000 project households in Guangxi affected by the acquisition of about 3,000 mu. ICIJ's own method page states what its figures count: it looked for what Bank documents call project-affected people, searching them for the words "affected", "PAP" or "displaced"; where a document counted only households it looked up an average household size; it decided to include all impacts, temporary ones among them, and says the impact counted "can be as modest as losing less than 1 percent of their land or income". It drew mainly on resettlement plans written before the work was done. Its data stops at 31 December 2014.
